newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE WEEKEND PROGRAMME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE WEEKEND PROGRAMME.

text.p: English premier league matches scheduled this weekend (league positions in brackets; all kick-off times GMT):

Stuart Pearce, Forest's inspirational defender, is set to return after a back problem and prove his fitness for England's World Cup trip to Georgia next week. Villa will miss goalkeeper Mark Bosnich, out for a month with a knee injury.

Derby skipper Igor Stimac, booked six times this season, starts a three-match ban, presenting an opportunity for Dean Yates to return after injury. Kevin Poole stands in for Leicester's regular goalkeeper Kasey Keller, on World Cup duty with the United States.
Sunderland's Richard Ord, who starts a four-match ban, is replaced in central defence by Lee Howey. Classy midfielder Lee Bowyer is available for Leeds after missing nine matches with an eye injury.

United are likely to attempt to halt a run of three defeats with a re-shuffle, Norwegian Ole Gunnar Solskjaer starting up front. Chelsea's Italian striker Gianluca Vialli is still troubled by a calf strain so John Spencer stands by.

Southampton manager Graeme Souness won the manager of the month award following last week's 6-3 hammering of Manchester United. Wednesday, on the slide since being top after four games, wait for a fitness test on striker David Hirst.

West Ham defender Mark Bowen has joined Romanian forward Florin Raducioiu on the injured list and out-of-contract full-back Tim Breacker could return. Spurs have a thigh injury worry over winger Ruel Fox.

Leaders Arsenal will not relish a potentially tough fixture against Wimbledon who boast seven wins and a draw from their last eight matches. Arsenal's French midfielder Remi Garde, who made his debut last week against Leeds, is doubtful with a groin injury.
Scotland defender Colin Hendry could make a remarkable return to the Blackburn team only four weeks after a groin operation. Liverpool look for a seventh win in eight league matches.

Even without injured striker Alan Shearer, Newcastle are buoyant following their 4-0 win over Hungarians Ferencvaros in the UEFA Cup on Tuesday. Middlesbrough look for a first league win in six matches.
Everton will parade Nick Barmby, the England forward they signed from Middlesbrough for 5.75 million sterling ($9.2 million) this week. Coventry are without a win in five league matches.
